title: Astragaloside IV ameliorates cognitive impairment in heart failure rats via modulation of RAGE-ERK1/2-NF-kappaB signalling pathway.
authors: Teng, Yu; Pan, Weibing; Li, Yutong; Chen, Jiaxin; Liu, Shaojiao; Han, Xiaowan; Wang, Lei; Zhao, Mingjing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄芪甲苷IV通过RAGE-ERK1/2-NF-kappaB通路改善心衰大鼠认知障碍，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白结合而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cognitive impairment (CI) is prevalent in clinical patients with heart failure (HF). However, there are no effective pharmacological interventions for CI treatment. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) is the principal constituent of Astragalus Radix and effective in HF, but its action on CI after HF has not yet been studied. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Cognitive function was evaluated in behavioural experiments on male rats with HF. Transcriptomics and network pharmacology were used to identify potential pathways. Western blots, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), Elisa, and electron microscopy were used to validate changes in identified pathways, brain inflammatory cytokines, postsynaptic membrane glutamate receptors and levels of apoptosis. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation confirmed the binding ability of AS-IV and selected core proteins. KEY RESULTS: AS-IV improved cardiac function and disordered cardiac muscle structure in rats with HF. The advanced glycation end-products-receptor of advanced glycation end-products (AGE-RAGE) signalling pathway was the core pathway. AS-IV reduced the expression levels of RAGE, extracellular regulated protein kinases 1/2 (ERK1/2) and nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-kappaB). AS-IV also attenuated the expression of proinflammatory factors, increased the levels of anti-inflammatory factors, and up-regulated postsynaptic membrane glutamate receptor expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation showed that AS-IV had favourable binding energy with RAGE. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: AS-IV enhances cognitive function of HF rats by inhibiting the RAGE-ERK1/2-NF-kappaB signalling pathway to reduce inflammation and apoptosis and thereby improve synaptic function. AS-IV emerges as a promising candidate for the prevention and treatment of HF-CI.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：认知障碍（CI）在心力衰竭（HF）临床患者中普遍存在。然而，目前尚无有效的药物干预措施用于CI治疗。黄芪甲苷IV（AS-IV）是黄芪的主要成分，对HF有效，但其对HF后CI的作用尚未被研究。实验方法：在雄性HF大鼠的行为学实验中评估认知功能。采用转录组学和网络药理学识别潜在通路。使用蛋白质印迹法、实时定量聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）、酶联免疫吸附测定（Elisa）和电子显微镜验证所识别通路的变化、脑部炎症细胞因子、突触后膜谷氨酸受体及凋亡水平。分子对接和分子动力学模拟确认了AS-IV与选定核心蛋白的结合能力。关键结果：AS-IV改善了HF大鼠的心脏功能和紊乱的心肌结构。晚期糖基化终末产物-晚期糖基化终末产物受体（AGE-RAGE）信号通路是核心通路。AS-IV降低了RAGE、细胞外调节蛋白激酶1/2（ERK1/2）和核因子kappa-B（NF-kappaB）的表达水平。AS-IV还减弱了促炎因子的表达，增加了抗炎因子的水平，并上调了突触后膜谷氨酸受体的表达。分子对接和分子动力学模拟显示，AS-IV与RAGE具有有利的结合能。结论与意义：AS-IV通过抑制RAGE-ERK1/2-NF-kappaB信号通路，减少炎症和凋亡，从而改善突触功能，增强HF大鼠的认知功能。AS-IV成为预防和治疗HF-CI的有前景的候选药物。
